benefits.title: Keyword plus meaning
benefits.body: Built-in BM25 full-text search fuses with dense vectors in one hybrid search, so one vector store for RAG retrieves exact IDs and paraphrased questions alike.

benefits.title: Metadata filtering, multi-tenant RAG
benefits.body: Filter expressions (==, in, ranges and JSON paths) run with vector search in one request. Include the correct tenant filter on every request when sharing a collection through a partition key.

benefits.title: Answers stay current
benefits.body: Upsert replaces chunks by primary key, deletes remove them, and per-request consistency levels decide how fresh each read must be. No second index to keep in sync.

benefits.title: Large knowledge bases, smaller bill
benefits.body: Disk-based indexes, mmap and tiered storage keep most of a large knowledge base on SSD or object storage instead of RAM.

feature_blocks.title: Hybrid search for RAG, plus grep
feature_blocks.body: RAG questions mix meaning with exact strings: error codes, SKUs, clause numbers. Hybrid search for RAG runs dense and BM25 retrieval in one hybrid_search request, and pattern filters narrow both routes.
bullets: Fuse dense and BM25 results with RRF or weighted rankers
Regex filters (=~, !~, RE2) on VARCHAR, JSON strings and arrays; LIKE accelerated by NGRAM indexes
TEXT_MATCH, PHRASE_MATCH and TEXT_MATCH_FUZZY for term, phrase and typo-tolerant matching

feature_blocks.title: RAG reranking pipelines with Function Chain
feature_blocks.body: Since Milvus 3.0, a Function Chain runs an ordered rerank pipeline inside the search request, per segment, per query node and after the global merge, with no client-side requery round trip.
bullets: Blend vector score with freshness (decay) and popularity (weighted combine)
Call a model reranker such as Cohere, Voyage AI, vLLM or TEI
Sort and trim candidates; works in search and hybrid search

feature_blocks.title: Learning to rerank
feature_blocks.body: Train an XGBoost ranking model offline on relevance or click labels, register it with Milvus, and let a Function Chain score recalled chunks.
bullets: Features come from scalar fields: recency, source authority, usage counts
Native XGBoost scoring runs on query nodes, next to the data
Rule-based options too: boost ranker and decay rankers

feature_blocks.title: Disk indexes to cut cost
feature_blocks.body: Not every chunk needs to live in memory: HNSW for the hot set, disk and quantized indexes for the rest. Pick the footprint for your latency budget.
bullets: DiskANN keeps the graph and raw vectors on SSD; AISAQ moves nearly everything to SSD
mmap and tiered storage load data from disk or object storage on demand
Quantized indexes: IVF_RABITQ (up to 1:32 compression), IVF_SQ8, IVF_PQ

code.h2: RAG vector database example: tenant-scoped retrieval
code.intro: Store chunks with a tenant field, then retrieve the top matches for one customer and pass them to your LLM.
code.code:
# pip install -U "pymilvus[milvus-lite]"
from pymilvus import MilvusClient

client = MilvusClient("rag_demo.db")  # same code against http://localhost:19530 or Zilliz Cloud
client.create_collection(collection_name="chunks", dimension=768)

# embed() is your embedding model (768 dimensions here)
client.insert(collection_name="chunks", data=[
    {"id": 1, "vector": embed("Rotate API keys under Settings > Security."), "tenant": "acme",
     "text": "Rotate API keys under Settings > Security."},
])

hits = client.search(
    collection_name="chunks",
    data=[embed("How do I rotate API keys?")],
    filter='tenant == "acme"',          # retrieve only this customer's documents
    limit=5,
    output_fields=["text"],
)
context = "\n\n".join(h["entity"]["text"] for h in hits[0])  # put into your LLM prompt
code.note: embed() is your embedding model. For BM25 + dense hybrid retrieval and regex filters, see the hybrid search and pattern matching guides.

faqs: Which vector database is best for RAG?
One that covers retrieval end to end: keyword plus semantic search, tenant filters, reranking, storage that fits the corpus. Milvus ships all four, open source, one API from Lite to Distributed.
Do I need a dedicated vector database for RAG, or is pgvector enough?

pgvector fits when the corpus is small and already lives in Postgres. A dedicated vector database for RAG pays off when you need hybrid search, filtered search at scale, tenant isolation and disk indexes; Milvus Lite keeps the start just as light.
Do I need Elasticsearch for keyword matching in RAG?
Not for retrieval. Milvus runs BM25 natively, adds regex, LIKE and TEXT_MATCH filters, and hybrid_search fuses keyword and dense results in one request.
Does Milvus handle chunking and embeddings?

Chunking stays in your loader (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Dify). Embeddings can move into the database: Embedding Functions (Milvus 2.6+) call OpenAI, Cohere, Voyage AI, Gemini and others on insert and at query time, so you store text and search with text.
Can I rerank RAG results with my own model, and how do I measure retrieval quality?
Yes. In Milvus 3.0+, a Function Chain can score candidates with your XGBoost model or call a hosted reranker inside the search request. Measure recall@k and NDCG on labeled queries before and after.
Can I run a vector database for RAG locally with LangChain or LlamaIndex?

Yes. pip install Milvus Lite for local RAG, then use the official LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack or Dify integrations; the docs also include a Graph RAG tutorial for multi-hop questions. The same code later targets a cluster or Zilliz Cloud.

Function Chain: released in Milvus 3.0.0 (release notes 'Function Chain reranking'; PRs #47919, #50786), L1 stage in 3.0.1 (#52745), Hybrid Search support in 3.0.3 (#53541), dynamic fields in 3.0.3 (#54011). PyMilvus API FunctionChain / FunctionChainStage / function_chain.fn (decay, num_combine, round_decimal, rerank_model, xgboost) ships in pymilvus 3.0.1+. It is a rerank/scoring pipeline, NOT an embedding pipeline. DOCS MISSING: milvus-docs v3.0.x has no user guide page for Function Chain (only release notes + roadmap) - confirm a doc page exists before launch, or link release notes.

Learning to rank: released as the native `xgboost` Function Chain expression (milvus #51317 in v3.0.0; design doc 20260708-xgboost-function-chain.md; issue #51192). Scope: L0 rerank only (per segment on QueryNode), UBJ-format XGBoost models registered as a FileResource, features = scalar columns in argument order, output raw|default. No training inside Milvus; no L2 support yet. Not documented on milvus.io (docs missing - confirm before launch). Copy says 'learning-to-rank' because the design doc frames it that way; we do not claim a generic LTR framework.

Grep: regex =~ / !~ (RE2) is labelled 'Milvus 3.0.x' in pattern-matching docs, targets VARCHAR, JSON string paths and ARRAY elements; NGRAM accelerates LIKE and eligible regex filters; TEXT_MATCH_FUZZY is 'Milvus 3.0.0+' in keyword-match docs. FMINDEX intentionally not mentioned.
Weighted RRF (per-request weights) shipped in 3.0.1 (#52926); copy just says RRF / weighted.

Docs label AISAQ (Milvus 2.6.4+), Tiered Storage (2.6.4+) and Boost Ranker (2.6.2+) as beta. Copy does not say beta; decide before launch. Memory facts used only as documented: DiskANN keeps PQ codes in RAM and raw vectors + graph on SSD; AISAQ keeps all index data on SSD; IVF_RABITQ docs state a 1-to-32 compression ratio; SQ8 = 8-bit ints instead of 32-bit floats.
